# Cross-language golden vectors for the `visio-seal-v1` envelope
# (one `key=hexbytes` per line).
#
# Generated from the Python reference implementation
# (python/visio_schema/crypto/envelope.py). Both
# python/tests/test_seal.py and the device-side C++ port load these bytes and
# assert that THEIR seal reproduces `seal_blob` exactly from the pinned
# ephemeral key, and that THEIR unseal recovers `seal_plaintext` from it.
#
# This is the most important fixture in the sealed-QR work. The device opens
# these envelopes with a C++ port against the RV1106's OpenSSL 1.1.1h, and a
# drift between the two implementations does not fail loudly in CI — it fails
# in a factory, where the symptom is "the QR doesn't work" on a rig somebody
# already shipped. Pinning both directions against committed bytes turns that
# into a build failure.
#
# The keys are deliberately recognisable counting patterns. They are TEST keys;
# the real fleet private key lives in gilabs-root/secrets/ and never enters
# this repo.
#
#   seal_private    X25519 private scalar, bytes 0x00..0x1f
#   seal_public     its public point
#   seal_ephemeral  the pinned ephemeral private scalar, bytes 0x20..0x3f
#                   (production mints a fresh one per envelope; it is fixed
#                    here ONLY so the seal direction is reproducible)
#   seal_kid        SHA-256(seal_public)[:4] — the fleet key generation id
#   seal_plaintext  a realistic sealed body: storage secret + a recording key
#                   + the previous one + an expiry
#   seal_blob       "VSL1" || kid || ephemeral_public || ChaCha20-Poly1305 ct
#   seal_empty_blob the same, sealing an EMPTY plaintext. Exactly the minimum
#                   legal envelope (56 B), and the case a device-side port is
#                   most likely to get wrong: with no ciphertext body there is
#                   no plaintext-decrypt call, so any length counter shared
#                   with the AAD step is still holding the AAD's length when
#                   the AEAD is finalised. Anyone can mint this against the
#                   published fleet key, so it is reachable, not theoretical.
#
seal_private=000102030405060708090a0b0c0d0e0f101112131415161718191a1b1c1d1e1f
seal_public=8f40c5adb68f25624ae5b214ea767a6ec94d829d3d7b5e1ad1ba6f3e2138285f
seal_ephemeral=202122232425262728292a2b2c2d2e2f303132333435363738393a3b3c3d3e3f
